title: Food for the belly, blows for the back
odia:
ପେଟକୁ ଦେଇ
ପିଠିକି ମାଇଲେ ସୁହାଉ ଥାଇ।
literal_meaning: Having given to the belly, if one strikes the back, it remains agreeable.
meaning_odia: ପେଟକୁ ଖାଇବା ଦେଇ ପିଠିରେ ମାଡ଼ ମାରିଲେ ମଧ୍ୟ ତାହା ସୁହାଏ ବୋଲି ପଙ୍କ୍ତିର ବକ୍ତା କହୁଛନ୍ତି। ଆମ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପାଠରେ ଖାଦ୍ୟ ବା ଜୀବିକା ପାଇଁ ନିର୍ଭରତା ଭିତରେ ଅପମାନ ଓ କଷ୍ଟ ସହିବାର ଇଙ୍ଗିତ ଅଛି। ଖାଇବା ଦେବା ଦ୍ୱାରା କାହାକୁ ମାଡ଼ ମାରିବାର ଅଧିକାର ମିଳେ—ଏପରି ମତକୁ ଏହି ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ସମର୍ଥନ କରୁନାହିଁ।
explanation: The saying places nourishment and a blow in the same exchange. Its speaker claims that feeding makes even the blow acceptable. Read critically, the image can expose how dependence for sustenance makes harsh treatment something a person endures. That is an editorial interpretation of the contrast, not a justification for the treatment.
usage_example: Original imagined example: In a discussion of dependence, someone quotes the belly-and-back saying. Another participant points out that providing food cannot excuse humiliating or hurting the person who needs it.
cultural_context: Belly and back give the exchange two bodily locations: the belly receives sustenance, the back receives the blow. The source leaves both people unnamed, allowing the contrast to be discussed without assigning it to a particular household or occupation.
